To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MetaCyc database is a collection of nonredundant, experimentally validated metabolic pathways and enzymes, curated by expert biochemists and molecular biologists.
MetaCyc is an important resource for microbial and plant metabolism, and is used in conjunction Pathway Tools to create a large number of organism-specific metabolic databases.
MetaCyc contains 1,700 pathways from 1,800 organisms, and 3,200 enzymes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: 1. The curation and maintenance of the MetaCyc database.

(1) curation of MetaCyc; (2) development and use of the Pathway Tools software for analysis of the MetaCyc database; (3) use of the MetaCyl database for genome analysis; (4) use of the BioCyc website for analysis of PGDBs; and (5) use of BioCyc for analysis of the human metabolic system.
the development of computational tools for the analysis, prediction and visualization of metabolic networks and their use for understanding the function of organisms and for metabolic engineering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MetaCyc is the most comprehensive and authoritative collection of pathways and enzymes in the public domain.
MetaCyc is an excellent resource of information on the metabolic pathways and enzymatic reactions of microorganisms and plants.

MetaCyc provides a comprehensive and detailed collection of pathways and enzymes, and that the Pathway Tools software provides a convenient way to query the pathways, visualize them, and predict metabolic networks from genome sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created the first set of high quality PGDBs for 165 organisms.
we have developed a system for predicting metabolic pathways from genome sequences that is accurate enough to be used for a large number of organisms.
we have developed a database of microbial and plant metabolic pathways and a software tool for genome annotation that can be applied to any organism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MetaCyc database is a useful resource for researchers and educators interested in the metabolism and molecular biology of microbes and plants.
the BioCyc collection of 165 PGDBs provides an unprecedented resource for studying metabolism in bacteria and plants.
the MetaCyc database is a useful resource for the analysis of metabolic pathways and the enzymes involved in these pathways.
